'Association for Movement Games Stuttgart 1893'), commonly known as **VfB Stuttgart** (German pronunciation:  ⓘ), is a German professional sports club based in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg. The club's football team is currently part of Germany's first division, the Bundesliga. VfB Stuttgart has won the national championship five times, most recently in 2006–07, the DFB-Pokal four times and the UEFA Intertoto Cup a record two times. In the all-time Bundesliga table the club sits in fourth place. Second team side VfB Stuttgart II currently plays in the 3. A membership-based club with over 100,000 members, VfB is the largest sports club in Baden-Württemberg and the eighth-largest football club in Germany. In 1973, the team qualified for the UEFA Cup for the first time and advanced to the semi-finals of the 1974 tournament where they were eliminated by eventual winners Feyenoord (1–2, 2–2).

title: VfB Stuttgart（A German football club.）_Baiduwiki
content: VfB Stuttgart (commonly known as Stuttgart) is a professional football club based in Stuttgart, Germany, that competes in the Bundesliga and plays its home matches at the Neckar Stadium. On September 9, 1893, the club's predecessor, FV Stuttgart 1893, was officially founded. Shortly after the merger, Stuttgart was promoted to the Southern regional league, one of the highest-level leagues in Germany at the time. In the 1926-27 season, Stuttgart won the Württemberg-Baden regional league championship for the first time. In the 1945-46 season, Stuttgart won the Southern Oberliga championship. In 1973, Stuttgart made its European debut, reaching the semi-finals of the UEFA Cup. In the 1974-75 season, Stuttgart finished 16th in the Bundesliga and was relegated to the 2. In the 1983-84 season, Stuttgart won the German top-flight league championship again after a 32-year wait. In the 1991-92 season, Stuttgart won its fourth German top-flight league championship. In the 2023-24 season, Stuttgart finished as runners-up in the Bundesliga.
